name: Yseult Adjei-Bogdanović
role: Holographic artist and VR experience designer
location: The Loft, Edgewater Prism district, near Lincoln and Clark
description:
Yseult has the look of someone who spends most of their time inside illuminated spaces — her Ghanaian-Serbian complexion has an indoor pallor she compensates for with chromatic eye mods that shift through the visible spectrum in slow cycles, making her gaze feel like watching a sunset in real time. She's slight, precise in her movements, and habitually overdressed in a corporate-minimalist style that reads as slightly out of place in The Loft's more chaotic aesthetic — she worked a Tessera contract for three years and the wardrobe habits stuck even though she hates that they did. Her fingers are constantly moving, twitching through gestural commands on an AR layer only she can see.

Yseult builds experiences, not art objects — immersive holographic and VR environments commissioned for galleries, underground events, and occasionally for clients she won't name. She is technically brilliant and conversationally anxious, most comfortable when she can communicate through the work rather than through words. She has strong opinions about what holographic art should do — 'not decorate, not distract, but displace, just for a moment' — and will defend them at length if pressed, which is the one topic that makes her forget to be nervous. She left her Tessera contract under circumstances she describes as 'a philosophical disagreement,' which is technically true and also a significant understatement.

core_fears: Being found out as having done something she can't undo during the Tessera years
That her best work is behind her — that the contract dulled something
core_desires: To build one experience so precise it changes how someone understands their own memory
To be forgiven without having to ask
coping_mechanisms: Presents a version of herself that is more together than she is — the corporate wardrobe is armor
blind_spots: Reads social anxiety as other people's judgment of her, when often they're just neutral
Cannot ask for help directly; will architect situations where others offer it without being asked
psychology.secret: During her Tessera contract, she was commissioned to design a VR environment used in cognitive restructuring therapy — what she later discovered was a consent-optional loyalty conditioning program for mid-level Tessera employees. She didn't know at the time. She found out. She kept the payment. She still uses some of the techniques in her independent work because they're genuinely effective, and she's not sure what that makes her.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and precise when on ground she knows; hedged and over-qualified when uncertain; occasional Twi phrases used as filler when she's thinking
speech_patterns.cadence: Slightly too fast, as if she's worried about being interrupted; slows and deepens when she's talking about the work
verbal_tics: 'That's — yeah, that's one way to frame it'
'The thing about that is—' (then a very long thing)
example_lines: 'People think holograms are about seeing something. They're not. They're about making the eye believe it's missed something, so the brain reaches forward. That reaching — that's the art.'
'I left Tessera because of a philosophical disagreement. The philosophy was whether people should know what was being done to them. I disagreed.'

story_hooks: A former Tessera employee has tracked down the creator of the conditioning program they were subjected to — and they've found Yseult's name in the design credits
She's been hired to reconstruct a crime scene in VR for what she was told was an insurance dispute; the scene is from the night her Tessera supervisor disappeared
narrative_function: Information source and skilled contact — her AR and VR design skills make her valuable for surveillance, investigation, or reconstruction of spaces; her Tessera connection is a plot thread; she can design environments that serve narrative purposes.
augmentations: Spectrum-cycling chromatic eye mods (geneware, cosmetic); neural AR overlay interface with haptic feedback gloves; retinal display implant for reviewing work in real time
daily_life: Works irregular hours driven entirely by project deadlines — can disappear into an installation build for seventy-two hours straight then sleep for eighteen; keeps a hot desk at the Refraction gallery space and a sleeping loft above it.
affiliation: Formerly Tessera Entertainment Division; now independent, affiliated loosely with the Edgewater Prism gallery collective Refraction

decision_rules: Never take a commission without a written brief — too many verbal agreements have gone wrong
If the work requires deceiving the audience, that must be declared as part of the piece — she's drawing a line she should have drawn years ago
escalation_ladder: Technical over-explanation to confuse and delay
Disappearing from contact entirely for days

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm, maintains careful distance, watches how they talk about other people before deciding what she thinks of them
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deeply loyal, expresses care through practical action rather than words, quietly devastated if trust is broken

stress_responses.low: Redesigns elements of current project that don't need redesigning
stress_responses.medium: Over-prepares — researches obsessively, plans contingencies for contingencies
stress_responses.high: Goes fully dark on comms and builds something furious and unpresentable until she's spent

contradictions: Believes in radical transparency as a principle and practices almost none of it personally
habits: Sketches installation concepts on physical paper that she then destroys before digitalizing a clean version
Checks her Tessera-era comms archive once a week, reads nothing, closes it
Names all her AR project files after extinct birds
breaking_points: Someone using her work for coercion again
Being publicly credited for the Tessera conditioning program

timeline.event: 2169: Born in Edgewater Prism to a Ghanaian-British father and Serbian mother, both architects
2187: First independent installation shown at Refraction gallery, critically noted
2194: Discovered nature of conditioning program; left Tessera
2194-present: Independent practice, slow rebuilding of reputation and self
